figures.title: The memguard loop: floor, SIGKILL, reload, retry
figures.caption: Unified memory makes the footprint one shared number: 111.5 GB across the pair, roughly 55.8 GB per rank, and no separate VRAM to spill into. memguard.sh polls MemAvailable; below 2.5 GiB it sends SIGKILL, which cannot be caught, so the rank does not flush caches or close sockets. The kernel closes the sockets, in-flight requests get a connection reset, the launcher restarts the rank, and the shard reloads from disk before the client's retry can succeed.
figures.alt: Five lanes across six steps. The footprint lane starts at 111.5 GB, grows with the KV pool, then reloads a 55.8 GB shard after the kill. The MemAvailable lane starts above 2.5 GiB, falls, is sampled, crosses below the floor and recovers. The memguard lane reads a timer, decides, and sends SIGKILL. The rank lane serves, allocates, dies and restarts. The client lane sees a connection reset and retries.

data.note: The engine's device_memory_bytes gauge reads 111,515,771,428 bytes, about 55.8 GB per rank, covering weights, caches and live streams. The KV pool is 262,144 positions at 921.6 bytes per position, so the pool is not what crosses the floor; growth in live streams and the page cache is. SIGKILL is the point: a graceful stop would let the rank release the pool, and the floor exists to keep the host from thrashing before that can happen.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to run the kill-and-restart loop.

steps.label: Steady state: the pair's footprint is 111.5 GB, about 55.8 GB per rank.
The KV pool grows as streams hold context.
memguard.sh reads MemAvailable on a timer.
SIGKILL: the rank cannot catch it or flush its caches.
The launcher restarts the rank, reloads the shard, and the client retries.

figures.title: Four streams: 1.80× aggregate, 45% of the linear ceiling
figures.caption: Measured decode on the pair: one stream 59.1 tok/s, four streams 106.2 tok/s aggregate, a 1.80× multiplier, and 26.55 tok/s per stream. The linear prediction is 4 × 59.1 = 236.4 tok/s; the measured aggregate reaches 45% of it, so batching is sublinear. The per-stream rate is also 45% of the single-stream rate, which is the same shortfall seen from the other side.
figures.alt: Four horizontal bars in tokens per second. One stream is 59.1. Per stream at four streams is 26.55. Aggregate at four streams is 106.2, marked 1.80 times. The linear prediction of four times 59.1 is 236.4. The aggregate bar is less than half the linear bar.

data.note: The shortfall has several candidate causes and the run does not separate them: the bandwidth ceiling N·B/(W+K), the 16-row decode kernel (ROUND_ROWS=16), the SM clock observed at 2,197 MHz against a 3,003 MHz silicon maximum, and the 120,000 ms cumulative pair stall. A roofline calculation can test bandwidth; the rest needs profiling or controlled experiments.

sources.note: NVIDIA DGX Spark hardware guide: 273 GB/s LPDDR5X shared between CPU and GPU, and the GB10's 3,003 MHz maximum clock.
